title: One Point Lesson - Seal Gas (N2 Buffer) Management (OPL-KC-4501-03)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-KC-4501-03 - Seal Gas (N2 Buffer) Management.

Equipment: KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 4500 - RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-4501 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-4501.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains seal gas (n2 buffer) management for KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR) in the RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM. The nitrogen buffer keeps flammable process gas out of the crankcase; loss of seal gas is a fire/explosion risk. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Verify FT-4506 seal gas flow is established before start
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Maintain the buffer differential above process pressure
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Watch the distance-piece vent for signs of leakage
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Respond immediately to a seal-gas low alarm
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Never run the compressor with seal gas lost
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: High discharge temperature trip TSHH-4503, capacity drop | Likely Cause: 1st stage suction plate valve fractured | Action: Replaced complete suction valve set, checked seat, leak tested
- Symptom: KC-4501 tripped on PSLL-4504 low lube oil pressure | Likely Cause: Lube oil pump gears worn, relief valve set low | Action: Overhauled lube oil pump, reset relief valve, verified 2.5 barg
- Symptom: High blow-by, low 2nd stage efficiency | Likely Cause: PTFE piston rings worn beyond limit | Action: Renewed 2nd stage PTFE piston and rider rings, honed cylinder

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The nitrogen buffer keeps flammable process gas out of the crankcase; loss of seal gas is a fire/explosion risk.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-4501: e.g. PSLL-4504 trips at < 1.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-4501 before working on KC-4501.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
